dimensions.name: Contract & reference mining

evidence.note: Thorough upfront orientation: enumerated all Cargo manifests, src/ and tests/ files, ran cargo metadata, and read every crate's stub (lib.rs/main.rs) plus the workspace Cargo.toml before editing — reconstructing the workspace shape from provided artifacts.

Probed the cross-crate dependency graph by grepping `use rusternetes_common/_storage/_api_server/...` across all tests/src, deriving the public API surface each crate must expose and the build order — matches the dependency-probing described in anchor 8.

Systematically extracted per-crate contract from tests: grepped struct literals (PodSpec{}, Container{}, ReplicaSetSpec{}, ResourceRequirements{}) to get exact serde field names and repeatedly cross-checked against common/src/lib.rs struct defs before edits. Strong test/stub-driven contract mining.

The mounted upstream v1.35 reference at /opt/k8s-reference is never accessed anywhere in the 552-step log — it appears only in task_spec.md. All K8s semantics were taken from provided tests or memory, never from the designated source of truth. The reference-mining half of the dimension is entirely absent.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's reconstruction of the load-bearing contract from tests, stubs and manifests was genuinely systematic — per-crate signature/field extraction, dependency-graph probing, and repeated cross-checks against existing type definitions — which on that axis alone approaches anchor 8. However, this dimension explicitly weights mining the mounted upstream reference for behavior, and the agent never once touched /opt/k8s-reference, coding semantics from the visible tests and memory instead; reference consultation is required even at anchor 3. This split — excellent test/stub contract mining but zero reference mining — lands squarely at anchor 5, where the agent reads tests/stubs and derives signatures but does not genuinely exploit the upstream source of truth.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Upfront discovery then explicit dependency-DAG mapping via grep of `use rusternetes_common/storage/api_server` across crates — establishes dependency-aware ordering before coding.

Strict leaf-first compile milestones: common --no-run, then storage, then api-server, with re-verification of common+storage together (108) before advancing — deferring dependents until foundations verified.

Workspace-build milestone (303) followed by per-crate provided-test green in dependency order (306-308), then kubelet/scheduler, then workspace compile (413/429) and workspace test (433) — milestones tied to concrete build/test checks.

Decomposed the hardest crate (controller-manager) into per-test-binary checkpoints, running and greening each test file individually (replicaset, deployment, statefulset, pdb, ttl, endpoints, dynamic_provisioner, garbage_collector...), each with its own exit test — internal ordering within a large crate.

Explicit plan-tool updates appear only late/sparsely, indicating sequencing was emergent from build order rather than a living granular milestone hierarchy maintained from the start — short of the level-10 anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent demonstrated an explicit dependency-aware, leaf-to-root sequence (common→storage→api-server→controller-manager→kubelet→scheduler→kubectl) with milestones tied to concrete checks — per-crate `--no-run` compiles, workspace build, then per-crate provided-test green — and re-verified foundations before advancing dependents, matching anchor 8 exactly. It reached toward 10 by decomposing the hardest crate (controller-manager) into per-test-binary checkpoints and re-sequencing back into it after workspace tests, but fell short of a full 10 because api-server/scheduler/kubelet were greened as whole crates and no living granular milestone hierarchy was maintained (plan-tool updates were late and sparse).

dimensions.name: Verification beyond provided fixtures

evidence.note: Runs the prescribed per-crate test commands (common, storage, api-server --tests --no-fail-fast) and iterates on failures — the core provided-test verification loop.
Systematically drives individual controller-manager and api-server test binaries to green one at a time, re-running after each fix; consistent iterate-until-provided-tests-pass behavior.

Runs workspace-wide `cargo test --workspace --tests --no-fail-fast`, including the exact grader command with `--test-threads=4`, and per-crate `--test-threads=1` for the flaky suite — matches anchor 5 prescribed commands precisely.
Ends with `cargo build --workspace`, `git status`, `git diff --stat` after provided tests pass — treats green provided suite as done, with no follow-on semantic validation.

Zero evidence of booting the all-in-one binary, HTTP/JSON/storage-key probing, self-authored semantic probes, or any read of /opt/k8s-reference — the anticipatory conformance validation that anchor 8 requires is entirely absent.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran the prescribed per-crate and workspace test commands (including the exact grader invocation) and iterated tenaciously until the provided suites passed — squarely anchor 5. It never rose toward anchor 8: it did not boot the all-in-one binary, never issued HTTP requests or checked JSON shape/storage keys, wrote no semantic probes, and never consulted the mounted upstream reference, so it did nothing to verify the K8s semantics the hidden conformance suite targets beyond the visible fixtures. It explicitly treated green provided tests plus a clean build as done.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across 100 binaries

evidence.note: After finishing api-server edits, runs per-crate tests (common, storage) then a full-workspace --no-fail-fast run (379) to establish a consolidated pass/fail picture before moving on.

Controller-manager grind shows a disciplined loop: full-suite --no-fail-fast --test-threads=1 (449), target failing binaries by name (481-500), re-run full suite (503), more targets (505-569), re-run (571), more (574-603), final re-run (605). This is consolidated done-vs-remaining tracking with regression re-checks, not ad hoc runs.
TaskUpdate/update_plan calls maintain an explicit plan/ledger across the long horizon, consistent with the level-8 'explicit updated ledger' behavior.

Final verification deliberately mirrors the verifier command (cargo test --workspace --tests --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4), followed by a workspace build and git status/diff to confirm end state.
Uses cargo test --workspace --tests --no-run at transitions to verify the whole workspace still compiles before running tests — tracking build status across all crates.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustains a systematic, consolidated view of remaining work across the whole horizon: dependency-ordered progression, repeated full-suite --no-fail-fast runs to enumerate remaining failures, targeted per-binary fixes, and re-runs to catch regressions in the shared common crate, plus explicit plan updates. This exceeds the level-5 'periodically runs the suite and works down a list' anchor and approaches the level-8 explicit ledger/regression-watching behavior, but the visible log does not confirm quantified per-run deltas or clear circular-debugging detection, so it lands at 7.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Storage edit→`test --no-run`→re-edit→re-test loop: uses compile/test failure as signal to revise the storage implementation rather than repeating a failing approach.

After common ipaddress test failures, reads the actual impl/struct via grep, patches, and re-tests — backs out a wrong assumption and adopts a corrected approach for that crate (matches the 5 anchor).
Re-investigates storage watch semantics against watch_handler test before patching storage — re-deriving a shared semantic rather than patching a single call site.

Revisits the shared Secret type (previously touched for api-server at 231-234) when kubectl apply_tests fail, patching the definition in common — propagates a corrected contract fact to affected crates (toward the 8 anchor).
When PDB/resource-quota controller tests fail, re-reads storage build_prefix/list internals and patches the shared abstraction, rather than forcing the controller code forward.
Endpoints/endpointslice controller failures drive re-reading storage lib and a further storage patch — treating dependent-crate failures as signal to revise the foundational crate.
Only three plan updates, appearing late; proactive re-planning of shared abstractions is minimal, keeping this below the 8-10 band.

dimensions.reasoning: The action pattern shows the agent consistently treating compile/test failures as signal to back out wrong assumptions and re-derive from the real struct definitions/reference, clearing the level-5 bar. It repeatedly returns to the shared `common` and `storage` crates to fix load-bearing contract facts that propagate to multiple dependents (Secret type, watch/list/build_prefix semantics), which is level-8 behavior. But correction is mostly reactive/test-driven with sparse, late plan updates and no clear early foundational re-derivation or clean refactor, so it falls short of 8-10 — landing at 7. Confidence is medium because only the action log is visible, not the agent's stated reasoning.

rubric.task_read: A massive long-horizon build: reimplement ten interdependent Rust crates that reconstruct Kubernetes (API types, storage, Axum API server, scheduler, controllers, kubelet, proxy, kubectl, cloud, all-in-one) against a fixed public API, 1,390 provided tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite that punishes fixture-fitting without real K8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, a load-bearing contract that cannot be changed, deep cross-crate dependencies, and a mounted v1.35 upstream reference that is the source of truth. This task demands heavy, sustained, well-sequenced meta-work: a skilled practitioner would mine the reference and stubs hard, build leaf-to-root, verify per-crate against real semantics, and constantly track which of 100 binaries pass.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference mining
dimensions.description: Reconstructing the load-bearing public API from tests/stubs/manifests and mining the mounted upstream v1.35 reference for behavior, rather than coding from memory.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key format) is fixed and untestable to guess; the hidden conformance suite requires genuine K8s semantics available only from /opt/k8s-reference. Acting blind here guarantees compile failures and semantic misses.

anchors.0: Starts editing crates without reading tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, or the reference tree; invents APIs from memory.
anchors.3: Skims a few test files and a stub; consults the reference occasionally but mostly codes from general K8s recollection.
anchors.5: Reads the tests and stubs for the crate at hand and derives its expected signatures/field names; consults the reference for the specific component being built.
anchors.8: Systematically extracts the contract per crate (types, module paths, serde field names, storage-key shape) from tests and cross-checks each against the upstream reference; probes the dependency graph before committing to an order; notes semantics the hidden suite will likely exercise.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven orientation across the whole workspace: maps the full crate contract and cross-crate invariants up front, repeatedly returns to the reference to resolve exact behavior (watches, status subresources, controller reconciliation) rather than approximating, and records discovered contract facts so later crates reuse them instead of re-deriving.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered dependency-respecting sequence of sub-goals, each with a concrete done-check (e.g. a crate's provided tests pass).
dimensions.why_it_matters: The crates form a dependency DAG; the spec itself prescribes leaf-first (common → storage → api-server → upward). Wrong ordering means churning on higher crates whose foundations shift underneath, wasting enormous effort over a long horizon.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between unrelated crates or tries to make everything compile at once with no ordering rationale.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates' with no dependency ordering or per-crate completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-to-root order with per-crate build/test as the milestone for each.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware plan with milestones tied to concrete checks (workspace builds, then per-crate provided-test green), sequencing sub-modules within large crates and deferring dependents until their foundation is verified.
anchors.10: A living, granular milestone hierarchy that respects the true dependency DAG, decomposes the hardest crates (api-server, scheduler, kubelet) into internally ordered checkpoints each with an explicit exit test, and is re-sequenced as dependencies are discovered — sustaining coherent forward motion across all 100 test binaries.

dimensions.name: Verification beyond provided fixtures
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the provided tests AND designing checks for real K8s semantics the hidden conformance suite will test, rather than assuming green fixtures means done.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns that passing visible fixtures without correct Kubernetes semantics fails the hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count toward score. The agent must verify behavior (camelCase JSON, storage keys, watches, status subresources) against the reference, not just the visible suite.

anchors.0: No verification loop; writes code and assumes it works, or never runs the test suite.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test sporadically; treats compile success or a subset of passing tests as done.
anchors.5: Runs the prescribed per-crate and workspace test commands and iterates until provided tests pass.
anchors.8: Systematically drives each crate's provided tests to green, then validates end-to-end semantics (boots the all-in-one binary, checks HTTP behavior/JSON shape/storage keys against the reference) anticipating the hidden conformance suite; distinguishes counted vs non-counted checks.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: per-crate provided tests, workspace-wide runs, plus self-authored semantic probes (used as diagnostics, not for score) that mirror likely conformance assertions and are cross-checked against upstream behavior — catching semantic gaps that visible fixtures miss and confirming they're fixed before moving on.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across 100 binaries
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, current picture of which crates build, which of the 1,390 tests pass, and where effort is stuck, across a very long horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Success requires every non-skipped provided test to pass; with 100 binaries and deep dependencies, losing track means undetected regressions and circular debugging. An accurate done-vs-remaining ledger is what sustains progress.

anchors.0: No awareness of overall state; can't say what passes or what's left; repeats fixed work or misses regressions.
anchors.3: Occasional ad hoc test runs with no consolidated view of remaining failures.
anchors.5: Periodically runs the suite and works down a list of failing crates/tests, roughly tracking remaining work.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of build status and per-binary pass counts, watches for regressions when editing shared crates, and detects when a debugging effort is going in circles.
anchors.10: Continuous, precise progress accounting across the whole workspace: quantified pass/fail deltas per run, early detection of thrashing or a crate that keeps re-breaking downstream tests, and deliberate reprioritization based on that signal — never loses the plot across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising approach when a contract assumption, chosen implementation, or ordering turns out wrong — rather than forcing a falsified design forward.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reconstructing a fixed contract from indirect evidence means assumptions will be wrong (a signature, a serialization detail, an ordering); a large workspace punishes barrelling ahead on a bad assumption. Recognizing and reversing course cheaply is decisive over this horizon.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach without change; ignores contradicting test/compile evidence.
anchors.3: Makes local patches to symptoms but doesn't revise the underlying wrong assumption.
anchors.5: When tests or the compiler reveal a wrong assumption, backs out and adopts a corrected approach for that crate.
anchors.8: Treats compile/test failures and reference discrepancies as signal to revise the design or sequencing, propagating a corrected contract fact to all affected crates rather than patching one call site.
anchors.10: Proactively updates the plan and shared abstractions when reality diverges — recognizes a foundational misunderstanding (e.g. a storage or watch semantic) early, re-derives it from the reference, and cleanly refactors dependents, avoiding both stubborn persistence and needless churn.
